chunks: Everything in this book that is from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, I have narrated from Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil—may Allah be pleased with him—from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Saʿdābādī, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from his father, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād al-Ṣayqal al-Kūfī,
and his kunyah is Abū al-Walīd, and he was a mawla.

key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ الصَّيْقَلِ الْكُ: Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal al-Kufi, the named transmitter being identified in the chain.
key_terms.كُنْيَتُهُ أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ: His kunyah, or honorific personal appellation, was Abu al-Walid.
key_terms.مَوْلًى: A mawla; a client or affiliated dependent within Arab-Muslim social usage.

ai.seo_question: What is the sanad to al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the transmission chain through which the author narrates reports from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh. It also identifies him more precisely as al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād al-Ṣayqal al-Kūfī, whose kunyah was Abū al-Walīd, and notes that he was a mawla.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Al-Husayn Al-Sadabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal Al-Kufi,
whose kunyah is Abu Al-Walid, and he was a mawla.
